summary: The bill amends Section 6409(a) of the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012 to require state and local governments to approve (or be deemed to approve after 60 days) any request to modify an existing wireless tower, base station, or telecommunications facility that does not substantially change its physical dimensions, including modifications that add backup power or hardening for public safety benefits, while limiting required documentation and allowing expedited federal court enforcement.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends federal law to streamline state and local government review processes for modifications to wireless and telecom facilities. It imposes deadlines, deemed approvals, and documentation limits on local governments but contains no provisions that authorize, increase, decrease, or otherwise affect any government expenditures or budgets.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, tax credits, deductions, or any revenue measures.
The bill addresses wireless and telecommunications facility modifications and has no connection to healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage, or regulation.
No provisions in the bill relate to firearms, gun ownership, or gun regulations.
The bill has no provisions concerning immigration, visas, border security, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address abortion access, restrictions, funding, or reproductive health services.
While the bill references public-safety benefits such as backup power on towers, these are civilian telecommunications improvements and do not involve military or defense spending or policy.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, emissions, land-use protections, or climate policy.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, housing subsidies, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill contains nothing about schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance regulation.
The bill does not alter sentencing, policing practices, or criminal-justice procedures.
No provisions concern tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or globalization.
The bill does not authorize spending, create new programs, or contain any fiscal measures that would affect deficits or the national debt.
No provisions address legal protections, nondiscrimination rules, or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill contains no foreign-aid authorizations, reductions, or policy changes.
No provisions relate to voting access, election administration, voter ID, or campaign finance.

The bill facilitates faster deployment and modification of telecommunications infrastructure by limiting local regulatory barriers. While this reduces certain local-government oversight of tech facilities, the legislation does not address data privacy, consumer-data protection, or broader technology regulation.
No provisions affect worker protections, collective bargaining, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil-rights protections, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination rules.
